context: Reactor destroyed by prompt criticality and steam explosion; 2 workers killed immediately (Valery Khodemchuk buried under debris; Vladimir Shashenok died hours later from burns); plant staff begin emergency response; fire brigades called; no external notification yet

Plant director notified; initial reports underestimated severity; dosimeters showed radiation but higher-range instruments broken; some early measurements showing 1000+ R/hr dismissed as instrument malfunction; Bryukhanov initially reported ~3.6 R/hr (actually 15000+ R/hr); Soviet notification chain begins

Government Commission established; senior Soviet officials flying to Chernobyl; military and civil defense mobilized; evacuation of Pripyat discussed but delayed; secrecy reflex dominant in initial response

protective_measure: No public warning given April 26 despite high contamination in Pripyat
context: 35 hours after accident: decision to evacuate made (evacuation not actual evacuation); April 26 was May Day preparation holiday weekend; Soviet leadership feared panic; children played outside April 26; residents unaware

protective_measure: Mass evacuation: 49000 residents evacuated in ~3.5 hours
context: Announcement gave 2-3 hours notice; residents told 'temporary evacuation for 3 days' (most never returned); ~1200 buses and 200 other vehicles; evacuation completed by 17:00 local; 36-hour delay = children received substantial I-131 thyroid dose; KI not distributed to Pripyat residents

protective_measure: Sweden begins investigation assuming domestic source
context: Worker at Forsmark NPP (Stockholm area) triggered foot contamination alarm; initial assumption: leak at Forsmark; but all Swedish reactors normal; airborne particle monitoring detected Cs-137 Cs-134 I-131 Ru-106; Swedish authorities determine external source; first external detection 62 hours after accident
source: Devell L et al. 1986 Nature 321:192; atmospheric_transport_plume_REAL.csv

protective_measure: Sweden threatens to announce Soviet nuclear accident publicly
context: Sweden contacted Soviet embassy; Soviets initially denied any accident; under pressure (Sweden preparing official statement): Soviet authorities decided to make brief announcement; key diplomatic pressure forcing disclosure
source: Devell 1986 Nature; Swedish Radiation Safety Authority records; Barringer 1986 NYT

protective_measure: TASS bulletin: accident at Chernobyl power plant; measures taken; investigation underway
context: 2-sentence announcement: 'An accident has taken place at the Chernobyl power plant, and one of the reactors was damaged. Measures are being taken to eliminate the consequences of the accident. Those affected by the accident are being given assistance. A government commission has been set up.' Deliberately vague; 66 hours after accident
source: TASS April 28 1986; declassified Soviet documents; INSAG-7

protective_measure: Precautionary advisories issued; food/produce monitoring begins
context: All Nordic countries detecting significant radioactivity; Sweden highest (within 1500km); monitoring stations show Cs-137 I-131 Cs-134 Ru-106; Nordic authorities begin coordinating; restrictions on outdoor activities in affected areas considered
source: Scandinavian national radiation protection authorities; European deposition monitoring records; 03_european_airborne_REAL.csv

context: Poland distributed potassium iodide to 18 million people (all children under 16 and pregnant women); based on rapid assessment that I-131 from Chernobyl plume posed significant thyroid risk; cost: essentially zero (KI is cheap); resulted in dramatically lower thyroid dose uptake in Polish population compared to USSR where no KI was distributed
source: Mettler FA 2007; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv; Cardis 2006; IAEA 2006 Chernobyl Forum

context: IAEA formally notified April 29 (3 days after accident); per 1986 IAEA Convention on Early Notification of a Nuclear Accident (not yet ratified); IAEA Director Blix requested information; Soviet cooperation was slow initially; IAEA had no authority to demand more information under 1986 conventions
source: IAEA 1986 Early Notification Convention; Blix H IAEA Director 1986 statements

protective_measure: Infant_formula_restrictions; milk_monitoring; vegetable_bans in some areas
context: West Germany ordered: no fresh milk to children under 2; spinach and leafy vegetables removed; Germany's contamination was from May 1 second plume (first plume went north); Austria suspended use of fresh milk and vegetables; Switzerland issued similar restrictions; all based on gamma monitoring showing elevated I-131
source: German Federal Health Office; Austrian OEVS; European deposition monitoring; food_agricultural_contamination_REAL.csv

protective_measure: No protective actions taken for Kiev residents
context: Soviet authorities allowed May Day parade (May 1) in Kiev to proceed normally; ~100000 participants in parade; Kiev only 100km from Chernobyl; Soviet officials had access to contamination data showing elevated I-131 in Kiev but did not cancel; subsequent thyroid dose assessments showed elevated doses in Kiev children
source: Soviet government decisions; Scherbak 1989; IAEA Forum 2006

protective_measure: EEC Regulation 1707/86: Chernobyl-specific emergency food limits
context: EU (then EEC) issued first pan-European emergency food limits: Cs-137+134 in fresh milk ≤500 Bq/kg; in other foodstuffs ≤925 Bq/kg; Regulation 1707/86 took effect; later revised multiple times; these were emergency limits derived from normal EURATOM food limits adjusted for short-term emergency

protective_measure: Restrictions on sale/movement of sheep from North Wales and Cumbria (Lake District)
context: Heavy Chernobyl deposition during May 1-2 rainfall over North Wales and Cumbria; Cs-137 in sheep meat exceeded limits; restrictions affected ~9000 farms and 4 million sheep; initially described as temporary; some restrictions in Wales not lifted until 2012 (26 years); UK restriction was more long-lasting than most European measures due to acid soil chemistry concentrating Cs-137 in vegetation
source: UK Ministry of Agriculture Fisheries and Food (MAFF); food_agricultural_contamination_REAL.csv; soil_plant_transfer_factors_REAL.csv

protective_measure: Most comprehensive public Soviet disclosure to date
context: Academician Valery Legasov led Soviet delegation to IAEA post-accident review meeting Vienna August 25-29 1986; 6-hour Soviet presentation was most detailed public account of accident; acknowledged design flaws for first time; presented operator errors as primary cause (later revised by INSAG-7 1992 to include design flaws); Legasov later committed suicide April 26 1988 (2nd anniversary) leaving tape recordings criticizing Soviet system
source: IAEA INSAG-1 1986 (Legasov report basis); INSAG-7 1992 revision; Legasov VP diaries/tapes

protective_measure: IAEA Convention on Early Notification of Nuclear Accident entered into force
context: In direct response to Soviet 66-hour delay in notifying international community: IAEA Convention on Early Notification of Nuclear Accident ratified September 26 1986 (exactly 3 months after Legasov report); requires states to immediately notify IAEA of any nuclear accident with potential transboundary impact; binding on signatories
source: IAEA Early Notification Convention INFCIRC/335 1986; IAEA Emergency Preparedness framework

context: INSAG-7 (1992): revised from INSAG-1 (1986); INSAG-7 acknowledged that RBMK design flaws (positive void coefficient; graphite tip positive reactivity spike) were equal contributor to accident alongside operator violations; INSAG-1 had placed primary blame on operators; revision was diplomatically significant - acknowledged Soviet design failure

protective_measure: Final closure ceremony with international witnesses
context: December 15 2000 00:00 UTC: Unit 3 shut down permanently; Ukrainian President Kuchma performed symbolic shutdown; attended by: EU representatives; G8 member states; Ukrainian government; international media; ending 14 years of electricity generation at the world's most notorious nuclear site; see chernobyl_unit_operations_REAL.csv for full Unit 1-3 history
source: chernobyl_unit_operations_REAL.csv; WNA; multiple news sources December 2000
